Summary

  • Republish the material as your own prompt pack, course, or toolkit, including lightly edited or AI-rewritten versions
  • Offer access to the original files as a bonus, lead magnet, or membership perk

Teams and agencies

This is a single-user licence. It covers one individual. If more than one person at your organisation needs to use the files directly, each needs their own licence. Get in touch about multi-seat terms.

The product is licensed, not sold. We retain copyright in the files. You own everything you create with them.

agency_product.descriptionHtml:
Turn Claude Code Into Your Client Delivery System.

A complete operating system for freelancers and agencies to discover, scope, propose, build, review, launch, hand off and retain website clients — as Claude Code commands that read one set of files per client and write into them, with a person between every draft and the client. Not a folder of proposal prompts: 21 modules, 37 commands, 29 templates plus a client-project skeleton, 17 checklists, 12 report shapes, 3 worksheets, four small scripts, and one complete fictional engagement to read before you run your own.

The problem

Most developers know how to build a website. The engagement around it is where the money and the reputation go: a proposal improvised the night before, a scope that said “and anything else needed”, an estimate that was a guess, revisions that never end because nobody counted the rounds, documentation that lives in a chat thread, a handoff that is a folder of files, and no process for turning a finished project into next month’s income. Each engagement starts from scratch; each one teaches the same lesson again.

Ask a capable model to “write a proposal” and you get the other problem: confident prose with invented requirements, a budget the client never stated, a promise about rankings, and a signature block that looks like a contract. Speed without a system produces professional-looking documents that are not professional.

The solution

A structured delivery system that runs inside Claude Code:

DISCOVER → SCOPE → PROPOSE → ONBOARD → BUILD → REVIEW → LAUNCH → HANDOFF → RETAIN
  • One set of files per client — client-config.yaml for the facts, CLAUDE.md for the rules, the scope as the contract, and four logs (decisions, assumptions, changes, risks) as the memory. Every command reads them; none invents.
  • Claude Code commands for every stage, each marked INTERNAL USE or CLIENT-FACING, each with its purpose, inputs, required context, steps, business rules, output format and validation — from /lead-qualification to /retainer-opportunity, with /agency-project-status as the one-block summary of any engagement.
  • Scope discipline as a habit: counts in the scope, an out-of-scope list before the price, acceptance criteria you can test, and /scope-change-check that classifies any new request in a minute with the reply drafted — calm, because it is arithmetic.
  • Evidence over confidence: audits with evidence and a five-level priority system, estimates as ranges with assumptions, readiness with proof, reports where every number names its source and missing data says unavailable.
  • The ten operating rules in every command: work within scope, never invent client facts, identify uncertainty, preserve what works, expose no credentials, document changes, validate before done, flag scope creep, promise nothing the evidence does not support, stay professional.

What is included

201 files, 21 modules, 37 commands, 29 templates, 17 checklists, 12 report templates, 3 worksheets, 4 scripts — about 56,000 words. Every number here was counted from the bundle at build time.

Module Covers
01-lead-qualification Fit score with reasons; the unknowns; the questions before unpaid discovery
02-client-discovery Six areas — business, website, conversion, content, SEO, technical; the report the client confirms
03-client-intake Assets and access with dates; the access inventory that holds no credentials by design
04-website-audits Technical, SEO and conversion audits; issue, evidence, impact, recommendation, effort, priority
05-project-scoping The scope document; counts; out-of-scope; acceptance; the scope check
06-estimation-pricing Low / expected / high with assumptions; the price arithmetic; seven pricing models
07-proposals Six proposal shapes; what a proposal must never do; Markdown to PDF without proprietary tools
08-client-onboarding One approver, one channel, the kickoff agenda, the day-for-day rule said out loud
09-requirements Twelve sections with a source per requirement; TBD as a value; traceability
10-project-planning Phases, milestones as acceptance points, client inputs with dates, the risk register
11-claude-code-project-setup The workspace and the context Claude Code reads; never overwrites
12-build-delivery Requirements → plan → implement → self-review → test → document → review; the definition of done
13-client-communication Status, questions, delays, review and approval requests in three registers; the weekly report
14-change-management Classify, four impacts, approve, log — not every change costs money; every change is recorded
15-qa Seven areas; PASS / PASS WITH ISSUES / FAIL; launch blockers named
16-client-review Bounded rounds; the package; feedback triage into six classes
17-launch Readiness with evidence — GO / GO WITH WARNINGS / NO-GO; the launch report
18-handoff The plain-language document; access transferred, yours removed
19-reporting Monthly reports where every number has a source and missing data says so
20-maintenance-retainers Services from evidence; the retainer builder; response targets that are not guarantees
21-client-offboarding The clean ending; the retrospective that edits the system; honest testimonials only

Plus .claude/commands/ with 37 slash commands, templates/ with 29 templates and the client-project skeleton, 17 checklists, 12 report templates, 3 worksheets, a reference set (project-type overlays for ten kinds of project, Shopify / WordPress / static workflows, pricing reasoning with hypothetical examples, the client data policy, the communication rules, twelve troubleshooting entries), four standard-library scripts, and examples/example-client-project/ — a fictional physiotherapy clinic’s redesign from enquiry to retainer, every file.

The commands

Command Audience Purpose
/lead-qualification · /client-discovery · /client-intake Internal → client Fit score; the six-area discovery report; assets and access with secure methods
/technical-audit · /seo-audit · /conversion-audit · /client-website-audit Internal → client Evidence-based findings; the combined report with an executive summary
/client-scope · /scope-change-check Internal → client The scope document; IN SCOPE / AMBIGUOUS / OUT OF SCOPE for any request
/project-estimate · /generate-proposal Internal / client A range with assumptions; one of six proposal templates filled from the files
/client-onboarding · /setup-client-project · /requirements-document · /project-plan Mixed The start: approver, channel, kickoff, workspace, requirements with sources, the plan
/delivery-workflow · /client-project-qa Internal The build loop against the definition of done; seven-area QA with blockers
/client-status-update · /weekly-client-report · /client-question · /client-delay-notice · /client-review-request · /client-approval-request · /client-meeting-summary Client-facing drafts Professional, concise, no blame, no promises; nothing sent automatically
/change-request · /client-feedback-triage · /client-review-package Mixed Four impacts and approval; six feedback classes; bounded review rounds
/client-launch-readiness · /client-launch-report · /client-handoff Mixed GO / GO WITH WARNINGS / NO-GO with evidence; the record; the plain-language handoff
/monthly-client-report · /retainer-opportunity Client-facing Sourced numbers; services the site needs, with evidence
/client-offboarding · /project-retrospective · /project-estimate-review · /case-study-draft Mixed The clean ending; the lessons as edits; estimate vs actual; a draft from facts only
/agency-project-status Internal The master summary. Phase, status, every stage, blockers, client actions, risks, next five actions; project-status.json

Use cases

  • Turn discovery notes into a professional scope with counts, an out-of-scope list and acceptance criteria.
  • Generate a proposal from a technical audit — findings become priority actions, priority actions become scope.
  • Detect whether a new request is scope creep, and reply in a minute without an argument.
  • Create client status reports in minutes from the tracker, with the client’s actions and dates in their own section.
  • Build a repeatable QA process that runs before every client review and again before launch.
  • Create a professional client handoff in plain language, with every access transferred and none of yours left behind.
  • Turn completed projects into legitimate maintenance retainers built from what the site actually needs.
  • Standardise delivery across every client project, and improve it with each retrospective.

Who it is for

Freelance web developers; small web agencies; DevOps and technical consultants; Shopify developers; WordPress developers; AI-first agencies; solo technical founders; developers entering consulting. It assumes you can build the site. It does not assume you have run a client engagement before — the modules are written for a first one, and the example is a whole engagement you can read end to end.

Safety and honesty

No credentials in any file, ever: access is granted by platform invitation and recorded as present or missing. No invented client facts, budgets or metrics: TBD is a value, and a report says unavailable rather than guessing. No promised rankings, conversion increases, revenue, or launch dates while an input is outstanding. Nothing is sent to a client by a command; a person reads and sends. Testimonials are asked for honestly and never written for the client; case studies use only the facts in the files.

And plainly: this is not legal, accounting or tax advice. Proposals are not contracts, scope documents do not replace agreements, retainer templates describe services rather than terms, and the pricing examples are hypothetical reasoning, not rates.

How it fits with the other six

This is the engagement layer. The other products are the technical layers it sells and delivers with, and each is separate — buying one includes none of the others.

With Price The engagement it makes deliverable
Website Launch System $19.99 Building client websites — the build inside the delivery workflow
SEO & Website Audit Toolkit $19.99 SEO audit engagements — the deep audit behind the audit-and-build proposal
Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit $19.99 Conversion optimisation engagements
Operations & Maintenance System $39.99 Monthly maintenance retainers — the delivery side of the retainer you design here
Website Migration & Replatforming System $29.99 Migration projects — the technical work behind the migration project type
Shopify Automation & Admin API Toolkit $39.99 Ongoing Shopify catalogue operations as a retainer

The first three are also sold together as the Complete Site Builder Stack. This product is not in any bundle; there is no automatic upgrade credit.

Delivery and licence

A single ZIP, delivered by download immediately after purchase. 201 files, about 240 KB — Markdown, CSV, YAML, JSON and four small Python scripts; nothing to install beyond Python 3, which your machine almost certainly has. A published SHA-256 checksum accompanies the download so you can verify what you received.

Licensed to one person for unlimited clients, including branding the client-facing documents as your own. You may not redistribute or resell it, or sell the templates as a competing product. Full terms are in LICENSE.md inside the archive.

What is not promised

No client, no signature, no renewal, no profit. The system makes each engagement clearer, more repeatable and better documented; whether a prospect says yes, what you charge, and how the project goes are yours — and it is built so that they stay yours and are written down.

claude-code-seo-website-audit-toolkit.descriptionHtml:
Who this is for

Developers, technical marketers and agencies who own a website that exists and is not performing in search. It assumes you can read a diff, run a command, and reach the live site. It does not assume you are an SEO specialist — most of it is aimed at the competent generalist who has inherited responsibility for how a site does in search.

If you are building a site from nothing, the Claude Code Website Launch System is the better starting point. This toolkit is for the site you already have.

What it is for

The failure mode in agent-assisted SEO work is not bad advice. It is a check that reports success because it never actually ran, in a report that reads as authoritative. You get a confident list, act on it, and nothing changes — because the crawler stripped query strings and never saw page two, or the checker was pointed at the source rather than the built output, or the audit fixed the findings in the same run and left no report.

Every prompt in here is written against that. They demand evidence rather than summaries. They forbid fixing in the same run, because an audit whose findings disappear into a commit is not an audit. And they insist that every check is proved capable of failing before it is trusted.

What is included

Fourteen modules, twenty prompts, four report templates and three checklists — 26,000 words of plain Markdown. Nothing to install, no account, no subscription.

Module Covers
01-technical-seo Crawlability, indexability, robots, sitemaps, canonicals, redirects, status codes, pagination
02-on-page-seo Titles, descriptions, heading hierarchy, alt text, content structure, duplicate metadata
03-indexation Why pages are not indexed, and what actually helps
04-structured-data Schema that describes what is visibly on the page, by page type
05-internal-linking Orphan pages, crawl distance, anchor text, cluster-to-hub structure
06-core-web-vitals LCP, INP and CLS diagnosed one variable at a time
07-accessibility-seo The overlap, with the two halves reported separately
08-content-auditing Decay, thin content, intent mismatch, cannibalisation, consolidation
09-google-search-console Coverage, URL inspection, performance analysis, and the API's traps
10-bing-indexnow Bing Webmaster Tools and IndexNow, including what submission does not do
11-platform-workflows Shopify, WordPress, Astro, static sites, custom applications
12-launch-validation Pre-launch, post-launch and migration
13-competitor-research Ethical research from public information
14-reporting Executive summary, technical findings, remediation backlog, severity matrix

The prompt library

Twenty prompts, each with a stated role, objective, discovery phase, constraints, evidence requirements, analysis, implementation, validation and deliverables. They are the part you will use most.

  • Complete website SEO audit
  • Technical SEO audit
  • Shopify, WordPress and Astro SEO audits
  • Search Console analysis, and Bing / IndexNow
  • Indexation troubleshooting
  • Sitemap, robots and canonical audits
  • Internal link audit
  • Structured data audit
  • Core Web Vitals audit
  • Accessibility and SEO overlap
  • Content gap and content decay audits
  • Competitor research
  • Launch and migration SEO audits

They are not variations on one another. Each addresses a genuinely different question and carries the platform-specific facts that make an audit right or wrong — that a Shopify sitemap cannot be hand-edited, that a WordPress SEO plugin owns canonicals, that an Astro site with no site in its config silently emits relative canonicals.

What using it looks like

  1. Open START-HERE.md. It routes you to one file based on your situation.
  2. Open that prompt, replace the bracketed values, and hand it to Claude Code.
  3. It runs a discovery phase and changes nothing. You approve what it found.
  4. It produces findings with evidence — the URL, the response, the exact markup.
  5. You fix things, in a separate session, with the validation command it gave you.
  6. You break each check deliberately and confirm it goes red before trusting it.

Supported platforms

Shopify, WordPress, Astro, static sites and custom applications each have their own workflow, because the things that go wrong differ. The general modules apply everywhere.

How the three products differ

SEO & Website Audit Conversion & Revenue Website Launch System
Price $19.99 $19.99 $19.99
Best for A site that is not ranking Traffic that under-converts A site you are building
Technical SEO Complete Not covered Included
Search Console and Bing Complete Not covered Summary level
Content auditing for search Complete Not covered Not covered
Competitor research Included Not covered Not covered
Conversion auditing Not covered Primary One landing-page workflow
Funnels and drop-off analysis Not covered Complete Not covered
Experimentation Not covered Complete Not covered
Analytics and measurement Search data only Complete Setup level
Conversion copy Not covered Complete Not covered
Reporting templates Included Included Not covered
Accessibility SEO overlap only Conversion path only Complete
Performance Core Web Vitals in full Conversion effect only Included
Planning and architecture Not covered Not covered Complete
Platform build prompts SEO workflows only Not covered Full build systems
Security audits Not covered Not covered Complete
Git, CI/CD, deployment Not covered Not covered Complete

All three are also sold together as the Complete Site Builder Stack, at less than buying them separately. Both figures are shown on that page. There is also a fourth product for the stage after launch: the Website Operations & Maintenance System covers monitoring, security, backups, updates, deploys and incidents, and is sold on its own. If only one column above describes your problem, buy that one — there is no advantage to owning a system you are not going to open.

They sit end to end: the Launch System builds the site, this toolkit gets it found, and the Conversion & Revenue Optimization Toolkit turns the traffic into outcomes. They overlap deliberately in two narrow places — the SEO material, where this one goes considerably deeper, and landing-page conversion, where the conversion toolkit does.

Buying one does not include the others, and there is no automatic upgrade credit. If you want more than one, buy more than one.

Delivery and licence

A single ZIP, delivered by download immediately after purchase. 55 files, 88 KB, all plain Markdown — nothing to install and nothing that expires. A published SHA-256 checksum accompanies the download so you can verify what you received.

Licensed to one person for unlimited projects, including client work. You may not redistribute or resell it. Full terms are in LICENSE.md inside the archive.

What it does not do

It does not access Search Console, Bing or any analytics platform on your behalf — Claude Code has no credentials for your properties and cannot get them. Where a workflow needs that data, it tells you exactly what to export.

It does not promise a ranking. Nobody can. And where the honest conclusion about a site is that the constraint is authority rather than optimisation, these prompts are written to say so rather than supply a list of small changes that would not move anything.

claude-code-conversion-revenue-optimizat.descriptionHtml:
Who this is for

Developers, founders and agencies who own a website that gets traffic and does not turn enough of it into revenue. It assumes you can read a diff, run a command and reach your live site. It does not assume you are a CRO specialist — most of it is aimed at the competent generalist who has inherited responsibility for a number that is not moving.

If nobody is arriving yet, this is the wrong product. Fix distribution first with the SEO & Website Audit Toolkit, or build the site with the Website Launch System. This one is for traffic that already exists.

What it is for

Ask a capable model to “increase conversions” and a fair share of what comes back is a countdown timer, a fake stock warning, and a confident prediction that the change will lift revenue by some percentage. None of that is knowledge. Two thirds of it is a compliance risk.

The other failure mode is quieter and more expensive: an audit that finds problems and fixes them in the same session, leaving a diff across thirty files, no report, and no way to tell which finding was real. Or a funnel analysis built on a purchase event that fires twice, so every number in it is wrong in the same direction and nothing about the output looks unusual.

Every workflow here is written against those three failures. Findings carry evidence and an honesty label. Audits change nothing. Tracking is verified in both directions before any number is trusted. And no workflow will tell you a change will produce a percentage lift, because nobody can know that in advance.

What is included

Thirteen modules, 70 workflows, 68 commands, six templates and four worked examples — 65,000 words of plain Markdown. Nothing to install, no account, no subscription.

Module Covers
01-core The master audit, the four modes, the finding format, prioritisation, evidence standards, the prohibitions
02-page-audits Homepage, landing, pricing, product, category, checkout, signup, content
03-funnels Funnel mapping, drop-off diagnosis, micro-conversions, traffic source fit, lead generation
04-elements CTAs, forms, navigation, pricing presentation, trust, objections, conversion copy
05-ecommerce The Shopify audit in depth, product detail, cart abandonment, checkout, merchandising, post-purchase
06-saas The SaaS funnel, onboarding and activation, trial to paid, packaging, demo flows
07-analytics Analytics audit, measurement plans, GA4, privacy-first tooling, event QA, attribution
08-experimentation Hypotheses, sample size, design, reading results, the log — and when not to test
09-user-behaviour Usability review, session recordings, surveys, voice of customer, choosing a method
10-performance-accessibility Performance and conversion, accessibility barriers on the conversion path, mobile
11-platforms WordPress and WooCommerce, no-code builders, JavaScript frameworks, what is fixable where
12-reports Executive summary, full report, quick wins, experiment report, client delivery
13-templates 30/60/90 roadmap, finding log, experiment backlog, measurement plan, copy brief, hypothesis

Plus commands/ with 68 ready commands in nine categories, claude-md/ with the section that makes the conventions automatic, and examples/ with four complete runs.

The method

Measure → Diagnose → Prioritise → Change → Validate → Learn. Each step exists because skipping it produces a specific failure, and the toolkit names them: skip measurement and you get opinions about a site nobody has data on; skip prioritisation and you get forty findings and no idea which one to do; skip validation and you get a change nobody confirmed worked.

Underneath that sit four modes, which is the convention that makes the rest work.

Mode What it does
AUDIT Analyse. Change nothing. Most workflows are this.
PLAN Turn findings into sequenced, estimated work. Still no changes.
IMPLEMENT Make one specific, named, approved change. Nothing else.
VALIDATE Check the change did what was predicted.

Never let one session both find and fix. Every workflow declares its mode in its first line.

What a finding looks like

Every finding uses the same thirteen-field format, and the field that matters most is the one naming its evidence class.

Label Means What to do
Proven problem Something is broken and you can reproduce it Fix it. No test needed.
Strong heuristic An established mechanism, observed here — not proof for this site Usually ship it, knowing what you know.
Experiment opportunity Plausible, unproven, reasonable people would disagree Test it, if you have the traffic.
Insufficient data You cannot tell yet, usually because measurement is missing Instrument it first.

Findings are scored Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort and banded into this week, this month, next quarter, and do not do. That last band is the one most reports never produce and it saves the most time.

The Shopify module

A generic audit sees a slow product page. This one reads the theme: it finds the four apps injecting scripts through content_for_header, the image_url call with no width serving a 2,400px hero to a 390px screen, the loading="lazy" that Dawn-derived themes apply to the first image in a loop, the checkout settings requiring a company name nobody uses, and the app pixel firing a second purchase event alongside the native one.

It also states what each fix requires — a theme change, an app change, a settings change, or a plan upgrade — because a recommendation a merchant cannot act on is noise.

What it will not do

It will not predict a percentage lift. Not once, anywhere. The honest form is: here is the measurement, here is the mechanism, here is the metric to watch and when we will read it. Every workflow says so, and a build-time check refuses to package the product if a prediction has crept into a file.

It will not recommend manipulative tactics. Fake testimonials or reviews, invented customer numbers, countdown timers without a real deadline, stock scarcity that is not tracked, hidden fees, drip pricing, pre-selected paid add-ons, cancellation harder than signup, confirmshaming, deceptive button labels, or tracking without the consent your jurisdiction requires. The list is explicit, and it is repeated in every workflow rather than stated once — because a prohibition at the top of a long session does not survive to the end of it.

It will not tell you to A/B test everything. There is a whole workflow whose job is to tell you not to. Most sites do not have the traffic for a useful experiment, and running an underpowered test is worse than running none: it produces a number, and the number gets quoted.

What using it looks like

  1. Open START-HERE.md. It routes you to one file based on your situation.
  2. Open 01-core/MASTER-CRO-AUDIT.md, fill in the bracketed values, hand it to Claude Code.
  3. It runs discovery and stops. You read what it found before it continues.
  4. It produces findings with evidence — the URL, the element, the device, the viewport, and how many attempts reproduced it.
  5. You score them, band them, and do the top one in a separate session.
  6. You validate it, then do the next.

If you only ever use the master audit and the prioritisation framework, the toolkit has done its job.

Platforms

Shopify has a dedicated module that reads the theme source. WooCommerce, Webflow and Squarespace, and JavaScript frameworks each have their own file, because what goes wrong differs and so does what is fixable. Everything else applies anywhere.

How the three products differ

Conversion & Revenue SEO & Website Audit Website Launch System
Price $19.99 $19.99 $19.99
Best for Traffic that under-converts A site that is not ranking A site you are building
Conversion auditing Primary Not covered One landing-page workflow

Experimentation Complete Not covered Not covered

Ecommerce and SaaS specifics Complete Not covered Build level
Conversion copy Complete Not covered Not covered
Technical SEO Not covered Complete Included
Search Console and Bing Not covered Complete Summary level
Content auditing for search Not covered Complete Not covered
Accessibility Conversion path only SEO overlap only Complete
Performance Conversion effect only Core Web Vitals in full Included
Planning and architecture Not covered Not covered Complete
Security audits Not covered Not covered Complete
Git, CI/CD, deployment Not covered Not covered Complete

All three are also sold together as the Complete Site Builder Stack, at less than buying them separately. Both figures are shown on that page. There is also a fourth product for the stage after launch: the Website Operations & Maintenance System covers monitoring, security, backups, updates, deploys and incidents, and is sold on its own. If only one column above describes your problem, buy that one — there is no advantage to owning a system you are not going to open.

They are designed to sit end to end: the Launch System builds it, the SEO toolkit gets it found, this one turns the traffic into revenue. Where they overlap, this toolkit defers rather than duplicates — full accessibility auditing is in the Launch System, search performance is in the SEO toolkit, and the workflows here say so where they stop.

Buying one does not include the others, and there is no automatic upgrade credit. If you want more than one, buy more than one.

Delivery and licence

A single ZIP, delivered by download immediately after purchase. 99 files, 213 KB, all plain Markdown — nothing to install and nothing that expires. A published SHA-256 checksum accompanies the download so you can verify what you received.

Licensed to one person for unlimited projects, including client work. You may not redistribute or resell it. Full terms are in LICENSE.md inside the archive.

What is not promised

No conversion rate, no revenue outcome, no percentage. The toolkit is explicit throughout that predicted lifts cannot be made honestly, and that applies to the product itself as much as to the reports you produce with it.

What you get instead is a defensible order of work, findings that carry their evidence, and a way to find out whether each change did anything.
